title: Cap. X Arg. IV: Vasquez's word-refuge — reprobation-as-destination-to-punishment may be in each one's power; we mean denied preparation of sustaining/raising grace (angels and men), which Vasquez himself says is not in our power
pass_a_gloss: Vasquez therefore, In 1. quaest. 23. disp. 95. cap. 9. seeks a lurking-place in the word reprobation, and answers that it is in each one's power to be reprobated or not reprobated, if the discourse be of reprobation which begins from destination unto punishment. But we (as we have often forewarned) by reprobation do not understand the destination of some singular person unto punishment, or the pre-damnation of the same, but the denied preparation of such grace as would have efficaciously sustained a standing creature, and led it unto glory, as is seen in the case of the non-elect Angels; or which would have efficaciously raised a fallen creature, and led it unto everlasting life, as is seen in the case of non-elect or reprobate men. And in this matter we have confessing (who in other things is adverse unto us) the Jesuit himself, whose words I will set down: Since to be Predestined is that that grace which God knew would have effect in us be prepared for us; and not to be predestined is that that grace be not prepared for us, and neither of these is in our power, it is effected that to be predestined or not to be predestined is not in our power. Wherefore for this cause we have said that it is not in our power to be reprobated, if reprobation be taken for the negation of grace. These things he. Ibid. pag. 709.
pass_b_english: So Vasquez (In 1. quaest. 23. disp. 95. cap. 9) seeks a refuge in the word reprobation, and answers that it is in each one's power to be reprobated or not — if the talk is of reprobation that begins from destination to punishment. But we (as we have often warned) do not mean by reprobation the destination of some singular person to punishment, or his pre-damnation. We mean the denied preparation of such grace as would have efficaciously sustained a standing creature and led it to glory — as in the non-elect angels — or would have efficaciously raised a fallen creature and led it to everlasting life — as in non-elect or reprobate men. And on this point we have the Jesuit himself confessing (though elsewhere he opposes us). His words: Since to be Predestined is that grace which God knew would have effect in us be prepared for us, and not to be predestined is that that grace not be prepared for us, and neither is in our power, it follows that to be predestined or not is not in our power. For that reason we have said it is not in our power to be reprobated, if reprobation is taken for negation of grace (Ibid. pag. 709).
source_text: Vasques igitur, In 1. quaest. 23. disp. 95. cap. 9. in vocabulo reprobationis latebram quaerit, atque respondet, Esse in potestate cujusque reprobari aut non reprobari, si sermo sit de reprobatione quae incipit a destinatione ad poenam. Sed nos (uti saepe praemonuimus) per reprobationem non intelligimus destinationem singularis alicujus personae ad poenam, vel praedamnationem ejusdem, sed negatam praeparationem talis gratiae, quae stantem creaturam efficaciter sustentasset, et ad gloriam perduxisset, ut cernitur in causa Angelorum non-electorum; vel quae lapsam creaturam efficaciter erexisset, et ad vitam aeternam perduxisset, ut in causa hominum non-electorum sive reprobatorum cernitur. Atque hac in re habemus confitentem (qui in aliis nobis adversatur) ipsum Jesuitam, cujus verba apponam: Quum Praedestinari sit gratiam illam, quam Deus novit in nobis effectum habituram, nobis praeparari; et non-praedestinari sit gratiam illam nobis non praeparari, et neutrum horum sit in nostra potestate, efficitur ut praedestinari aut non praedestinari non sit in nostra potestate. Quare hac de causa diximus, non esse in nostra potestate reprobari, si reprobatio pro gratiae negatione sumatur. Haec ille. Ibid. pag. 709.
